Up close: Rough, bumpy copper-orange relief, like hammered sand-cast metal or rock: tiny pitted grains with light speckle on top and darker pooled hollows in loose diagonal drifts. No green shows anywhere in the picture. From a distance: A warm terracotta-copper that looks rough and shadowed, with lighter and darker patches rolling across; it reads as raw cast copper or rusty plate. Measured spec (average): metal 180, roughness 169, coat 98. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, sides, hero panel.
Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, show car.

Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.

Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: the relief needs big panels to read
Hood and roof: wide flat areas show the drifting dark hollows
Bold cream or black numbers with an outline; small ones get lost in the pitted grain.
Big solid graphics, stencil numbers and stripes in black or cream: the bumpy base is loud, simple shapes hold
Pairs well with: dark brown, cream, black, forest green.
pitfalls: Not smooth polished copper: the surface is pitted and bumpy
Not verdigris: the described green creep does not appear in the render, only orange-brown
Avoid: small numbers over the mottling, next to bright chrome.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 180 (true metallic), roughness 169 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 98 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the mottling, next to bright chrome.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: big solid graphics, stencil numbers and stripes in black or cream: the bumpy base is loud, simple shapes hold; wide flames or tribal in dark brown: tonal match keeps it rugged
Patterns to avoid: other grunge textures like rust or crackle: they stack into mush; gradients: the colour range is already uneven
Spec overlays that work: a gloss clearcoat pattern to polish selected areas; avoid more grain overlays; the roughness is already high
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
